newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO pledges support to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: COSCO pledges support to Hong Kong.

text.p: China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO) said on Monday it would continue to use Hong Kong's superior port facilities and pledged to help maintain the prosperity of the territory after its handover in July.

"In the near term, no other port can take the place of Hong Kong," Chen Zhong Biao, chairman of both COSCO and its listed subsidiary COSCO Pacific Ltd, told reporters after addressing the Hong Kong Shipowners Association.
Chen is also chairman of the China Shipowners Association.
"After Hong Kong's return to China in 1997...Hong Kong's role and status as a free port and an international shipping centre will not be changed," he said in his speech.
"COSCO will seek to develop all its businesses and to devote its efforts towards Hong Kong's prosperity and stability."
Hong Kong returns to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
Talking to reporters, Chen stressed the superiority of Hong Kong's shipping infrastructure and service sector.
He would not elaborate on reports in the local press about the parent company's intention to sell as many as seven of its port operations in China to the Hong Kong listed company.
China-based COSCO is one of the world's largest container transportation and shipowning companies.
